controls.label: SPHERE/ZIMPOL · polarised dust, 2024
controls.title: Polarised dust around Betelgeuse in 2024
controls.description: The degree of linear polarisation VLT/SPHERE-ZIMPOL measured in the V band on 3 December 2024, in the colour map and on the zero-to-0.10 scale the paper prints it in, placed in the plane of the sky through the star and spread along the line of sight by the scattering-angle efficiency of polarised light. The patches are dust. The colours are the publisher's legend for a ratio, not the colour of anything. Depth is a stated convention, not a measurement, and nothing finer than the 16 milliarcsecond beam is in the data.
controls.summary: Measured polarised light from dust one to 4.5 stellar radii out; its depth is a convention.

facts.label: Colour scale
facts.value: Degree of linear polarisation 0 to 0.10, the paper's inferno map

facts.label: Depth
facts.value: Not measured; the spherical shell at 3.5 stellar radii that best projects to the measured profile

controls.label: Great Dimming clump · December 2019
controls.title: The dust clump of the Great Dimming
controls.description: The dust clump Montargès et al. fitted with RADMC-3D to the images of the Great Dimming, drawn from the numbers they published for December 2019: a sphere of uniform density south and slightly west of the star and between it and us. Its extinction is scaled so the line of sight through its centre dims the star ten times, as the paper reports for the southern hemisphere, and the light it scatters back is drawn faintly over that. This is a model fitted to images, not an image.
controls.summary: The published model of the dust that dimmed the star ten times in December 2019, drawn as the extinction it causes.

facts.label: Model
facts.value: RADMC-3D sphere of constant density, Montargès et al. 2021, Extended Data Table 3

facts.label: Centre and radius
facts.value: (−1.9, −3.0, +12.5) au along right ascension, declination and toward Earth; radius 6.5 au

facts.label: Dust density
facts.value: 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ g cm⁻³ in MgFeSiO₄ grains centred on 0.21 µm

facts.label: Optical depth
facts.value: ln 10 through the centre, the 10-times dimming the paper reports

facts.label: Epoch
facts.value: December 2019, the only optimised solution the paper reports

controls.label: VLTI/MATISSE · off-limb light, 2020
controls.title: The light outside Betelgeuse’s disc at 4 micrometres
controls.description: The same reconstruction that paints this star’s sphere carries a fifth of its flux outside the published disc. On the sphere that light is a flat plate behind the body; here it is given a shape. The disc and the first beam beyond it are removed, because inside the disc the sphere is drawn and within one beam of it the light is the star’s own edge smeared by the beam. What is left falls far too slowly to be that beam: the envelope that best projects to it is r^−7.9, five times better than the constant depth an extrusion assumes. The image spans 100 milliarcseconds, so this speaks for the inner envelope alone. Its colours are the reconstruction’s own heat scale, because this is the same quantity as the sphere.
controls.summary: The fifth of the reconstruction that lies outside the disc, given the shape that best projects to it.

facts.label: Drawn extent
facts.value: 1.19 to 2.36 stellar radii: outside the disc and its first beam, to the edge of the 100 mas field

facts.label: Share of the flux
facts.value: A fifth of the reconstruction lies outside the disc

facts.label: Colour scale
facts.value: The reconstruction's own heat scale, the one the star's sphere carries

facts.label: Depth
facts.value: Not measured; the steeply falling envelope r^−7.9 that best projects to the measured profile
